title: Preventing tearing-mode instabilities in a tokamak with AI
summary: A model trained only on past experimental data predicts instabilities up to 300 ms ahead, and an AI controller adjusted plasma shape and beam power to avoid them in a real DIII-D experiment. The authors call it a proof of concept on one machine and one type of instability; paper published in Nature on February 21, 2024.
organization: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory and Princeton University

evidence.tested: The reinforcement-learning controller was tested in experiments on the DIII-D tokamak, where it kept the tearing likelihood below a threshold, including under unfavorable conditions.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not state the prediction horizon and lists no other limitations; tearing instability is hard to forecast.
evidence.ai_role: A deep reinforcement learning controller, trained in a multimodal dynamic model of tearing instability, adjusted plasma operation to keep it stable.
